subject: Bifurcated return-path causing POST failures during private cutover
messages:
From: Jai Singh <j.singh@trilliumhealth.org>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: POST failures after private cutover — intermittent 502s

Connor / Redwood team,

We cut over the private VPC link to your appliance this morning (cutover window 06:30–07:00 PDT). Since then about ~1–2% of our POST requests to your ingestion endpoint (10.40.5.12:443) are returning 502/connection reset. GETs appear fine. We captured tcpdump on the app tier and saw a handful of retransmits followed by RSTs.

What we observed: 
- Client traffic enters over the trunk to your private edge, is SNAT'd at your edge, but return packets sometimes take a different APO/return-path via our transit router.
- Symptoms look like asymmetric return path + either conntrack timeout or MTU clamping on intermediate FW.

I attached a pcap (trillium-tcpdump-20260923.pcap) and an abbreviated edge config diff. Could you triage? We have a support window later today at 16:00 PDT if needed.

Thanks,
Jai Singh
NetOps Lead — Trillium Health

Attachments: trillium-tcpdump-20260923.pcap (pcap), edge-config-diff.txt (text)
From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: Jai Singh <j.singh@trilliumhealth.org>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POST failures after private cutover — intermittent 502s

Thanks Jai — sorry you hit this during the cutover. I pulled the pcap and skimmed it. Initial read: there are SYNs followed by SYN/ACKs then an immediate window-zero RST from the server side in ~40% of the failures; others show pure retransmit/retry before reset. A few notes:

- Possible asymmetric return path: our edge is SNAT'ing to an ephemeral pool, but I see return packets hitting a different next-hop Uplink which may not have the same conntrack state.
- MTU: I see MSS=1420 in one flow but large segs later; not conclusive.
- Security groups: no explicit deny seen in our edge logs for the client IPs, but I'll validate stateful rules on the private appliance and on the transit router.

Action plan (short term):
1) I will ask Karthik to check conntrack allocation and whether SNAT port pools are being exhausted for the ephemeral NAT.
2) We'll run an isolated traceroute + capture from the server to your IPs to confirm return path.
3) If asymmetric return path is confirmed, we'll add a sticky SNAT or route override to co-locate return flows.

Can you confirm the client IP ranges and the times of the failures you saw? We'll sync at 16:00 if needed.

-Connor
Connor O'Brien
Network Reliability, Redwood Inference

On Wed, Sep 23, 2026 at 08:12, Jai Singh <j.singh@trilliumhealth.org> wrote:

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Jai Singh <j.singh@trilliumhealth.org>
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 10:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POST failures after private cutover — intermittent 502s

Quick triage notes from the edge appliance: 
- Conntrack table shows spikes during the cutover; ephemeral port utilization reached ~92% on one node (we autoscaled but port fragmentation persisted).
- I see SNAT mapping churn: same internal flow mapped to different external ports across packets when requests are retried — that will confuse client-side load balancers and cause mid-connection resets.
- Firewall on transit-router (Trillium side) is not dropping packets, but the path change sends return packets to a different NAT box that doesn't have the mapping (as Connor suggested).
- MTU: the edge is doing MSS clamping to 1400 for VPN tunnels. The pcap shows retransmissions consistent with occasional large segments hitting a non-clamped path — increased retransmits then application-layer timeout.

Short-term remediation I recommend: 
- Apply port-pinning (sticky SNAT) for Trillium CIDR on the edge for the next 24 hours. This will keep the ephemeral mapping stable for retries.
- Add a /32 on our route table for the Trillium egress-facing IP to force symmetric return via the same egress appliance while longer-term BGP fixes are coordinated.

I'll prepare a one-line patch for marissa to push (low-risk) and coordinate with Jai for a scheduled change window (we can do now if they approve).

Karthik
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Jai Singh <j.singh@trilliumhealth.org>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POST failures after private cutover — intermittent 502s

Thanks Karthik — that aligns with what we see. We can approve the sticky SNAT and the /32 route for the affected egress IP (10.40.0.254).

Two asks: 
1) Please note the change in our change control: CHG-TRI-983. We'll apply the route override at 13:30 PDT and monitor for 1 hour.
2) We'll also keep the pcap capture running on our app node and send updates. If the /32 fix is successful, we can work on BGP path-preference / community tags for permanent fix.

Jai
NetOps Lead — Trillium Health
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Jai Singh <j.singh@trilliumhealth.org>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 17:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POST failures after private cutover — intermittent 502s

Update after the /32 route + sticky SNAT were applied at 13:30 PDT on 9/23:

- Trillium reported a drop from ~1.8% failed POSTs to 0.05% over the 1h observation window. Subsequent monitoring over the next 24h shows negligible recurrence.
- We validated with tcpdump and saw consistent 5-tuple preservation (no port-churn) and no mid-flow RSTs.
- Follow-ups: Karthik will open a Jira (JIRA-TRI-3456) to track the long-term fix (BGP community to prefer primary egress + remove /32 once communities in place).
- Operations note: we should add a small playbook entry for private-cutovers that runs ephemeral port utilization checks and sets short-lived sticky SNAT when port churn > 80%.

Thanks everyone for quick coordination. I'll leave the ticket with Trillium for now and mark as monitoring.

—Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
